title: Commonwealth legislative powers (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Constitution enumerates Commonwealth heads of power (trade and commerce, taxation, corporations, external affairs, etc.). Laws must fall within a head of power; otherwise states/territories may regulate residual matters.

title: Chapter III courts & judicial power (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: federal judicial power is vested in courts defined by Chapter III, shaping which bodies may exercise it. State courts can exercise federal jurisdiction when invested by federal law within constitutional limits.

title: Implied freedom of political communication (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: High Court jurisprudence recognises an implied freedom of political communication as necessary for representative government. Laws burdening the freedom must pass a structured proportionality test as articulated in case law.

title: States — residual law-making (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Australian states retain broad plenary legislative power subject to federal inconsistency where Commonwealth law is valid. Criminal, property, and contract law often remain primarily state-led.
